title: ork accepts slicer relay v11
lead: ork accepts slicer relay v11, its role prompts and engine follow v11's rules, and it reads the gate role and the stop rules from v11's JSON instead of special-casing them.
findings_note: owner contract review 2026-10-30 (slicer, adj, ork alignment); slicer s424 (relay v11 cleanup and bump)
boundary: **Not in this slice:** the contract pins (S24), adj's JSON contract (adjudicate S45), serving or translating an older contract, and any change to slicer.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
slicer v1.17 bumps the relay contract to v11 (`../slicer` s424, which lands after s391, s407, s409 and s412). ork accepts only v9 and v10 (`internal/roles/roles.go`, `acceptedContracts`), so engine start and doctor refuse a project once its slicer prints v11 (`internal/cli/upgrade.go`, `internal/engine/engine.go`). Owner decision 2026-10-30: one v11 bump in slicer v1.17, with this companion slice in ork.

**Blocked on slicer s424 landing.** The golden and the exact rule text come from its output; until it lands, re-read `slicer ai relay --json` from `../slicer` main and the final `RELAY_CHANGES` entry for 11 before claiming.

v11 changes ork must follow (as planned in s424; confirm against the landed text):

- No `cd` for every role, the read-only ones included; a resumed headless role runs in the slice worktree (slicer s391).
- Implementer re-anchors cited lines and runs a defect self-check before review: concurrency and handle lifetime, docs updated with the code, a test that fails when the wiring is removed (slicer s407). `prompts/implementer.md` already re-anchors; add the self-check.
- A small fix round may be re-checked by whichever read-only role holds the findings; non-blocking owner questions are asked as they arise; parallel slices gate once on the merged result (slicer s412, as settled there).
- A `blocker` owner question is a wait, not a stop: it leaves `stop[]`. `stop[]` entries gain keys. `roles[]` gains `gate` with `ledger_role` `gate` (slicer s424).

Alignment gap found in the same review: ork's engine falls back to the next row on an exit classified `error` (S169 notes: a Claude limit shows as `error`), while the v10 and v11 `vendor_limit` obligation says any failure other than a classified limit stops. Record this as a decision with `adj ask` (accepted deviation, or narrow ork's fallback) rather than leave it as silent drift.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/roles/roles.go`: `ContractVersion = 11`; `acceptedContracts` gains 11. Whether 9 stays is the owner's call at claim (recommend `{10, 11}`); record it under S142's `boundary.contract`.
- `internal/roles/prompts/*.md`: first line `relay v11`, plus the rule changes above (implementer, reviewer, gate, architect, ui, spec-check as each applies).
- `internal/slicercli/contract.go`: decode `stop[]` with keys; for v11 require `gate` in `roles[]` and drop the gate special case in `LedgerRole` for v11 (keep it for v10 while v10 is accepted).
- `internal/engine/`: the brief builders and round logic for the fix-round re-check and owner-question rules.
- `internal/cli/upgrade.go` messages if the accepted set's wording changes.
- `testdata/cli/slicer/relay-v11.json` recorded from slicer after s424 lands (decision 0047); keep `relay-v10.json` while 10 is accepted.
- `docs/boundaries.md`, `docs/guide.md`, `docs/glossary.md` where they name the contract version; CHANGELOG.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `CheckContractLine("Contract: relay v11")` returns 11 with no error; a version outside the set lists the new set.
- `RelayContract.Validate` accepts the recorded v11 JSON, refuses v11 JSON with no `gate` in `roles[]`, and still accepts the recorded v10 JSON.
- `LedgerRole("gate")` on v11 reads the contract's `ledger_role`.
- Each prompt's first line equals `relay v11` (the existing first-line test, retargeted).
- The implementer prompt names the self-check categories; each role prompt forbids `cd`.
- Engine start with a fake slicer printing v11 creates a run; with v12 it refuses naming the accepted set.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. After slicer s424 lands, record `relay-v11.json` from it and read its `RELAY_CHANGES` entry for 11.
2. Ask the owner whether 9 stays accepted, and file the `error`-fallback question with `adj ask`.
3. Write the red tests against the recorded output, then the code and prompts.
4. Update the docs listed in Files. Refer to slicer's commands; do not paste its contract text.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .` are clean. SPDX headers. No new dependency.
- `slicer check` and `adj lint` pass.
- [HUMAN CHECK] With slicer v1.17 installed, `ork doctor` is ok and one relay runs end to end on a scratch project.
